articles.title: Keith Schaefer, 73, Bus Driver
articles.deck: Friends remember Keith Schaefer for the many years of service to Cedar Hollow.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name. Born in Cedar Hollow in the years after the war, Keith Schaefer spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Keith Schaefer died in June at home on Copper Place, at the age of 73.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Cedar Hollow. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Crosswalk
body: To the editor: Please keep the crosswalk in the budget. Many of us on Dayton Road use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Dayton Road for 22 years, and I want to say what a difference Scout Troop 14 has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the February meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Please keep the crosswalk in the budget. Many of us on Dayton Road use it every week.
Rosalind Yates, Marsh Landing

articles.title: Council Delays Vote on Juniper Drive Bus Shelter
articles.deck: The vote came after 11 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Residents of Marsh Landing said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Letter: The Bike Repair Clinic on Laurel Street Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Laurel Street for 12 years, and I want to say what a difference the Stonebridge Trail Crew has made. Please keep the bike repair clinic in the budget. Many of us on Laurel Street use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting.
Beatrice Farrow, Marsh Landing

articles.deck: The program begins in January and is open to all students in grade 8 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for January. Principal Angela Varga said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the spring term. Students will meet on Friday afternoons in the Foundry Row fire house, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
